page: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is a burstable performance instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 CPU model running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results show average performance across several standard workloads, alongside some notable limitations. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests yield average scores of 1519.68 and 12133.02, respectively. Memory bandwidth is solid, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 472.63 GB/sec and large-block write speeds at 53.44 GB/sec. However, single-threaded performance is weak in certain areas, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 877.0 and a poor bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 7.11 GB/sec. For database operations, the instance performs reliably, achieving an average of 9.35 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 5170.54 in PassMark database operations.

As a burstable instance, the t4g.2xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that experience periodic spikes in CPU utilization rather than continuous high loads. The use of custom ARM-based Graviton processors delivers resource density and power efficiency advantages over traditional architectures. This instance is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations that can tolerate burstable CPU allocation. It is less suitable for heavy single-threaded processing, large-scale LLM inference, or workloads requiring dedicated local NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is a burstable, arm64-based instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 32.0 GB of RAM, a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor without local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate average performance for multi-core processing, database operations, and static web serving, though single-threaded tasks and LLM inference show weaker results. It achieves 9.35 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and an average of 12133.02 in stress-ng multi-core tests. This instance provides a cost-efficient option for workloads with variable CPU demands, such as web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale database applications.
